❄ Yukon is more than a land of extreme cold and endless wilderness. It's a place where history, nature, and human resilience come together.
🌌 Would you ever consider living somewhere this remote?
If you enjoyed this journey, please like the video and subscribe for more extraordinary places around the world! 🌍

comments.author: @HelloPutinHere
comments.text: please dont give up, i love your effort and i want you to know that i really admire the serious way to work

replies.author: @EpicEarthYTB
replies.text: I can't tell you how much I needed to hear this today. 🙏 Truthfully, it can get very discouraging and lonely when you pour your soul into a project and feel like the algorithm just overlooks it. I’ve had moments where I seriously questioned whether I should keep going. But words of encouragement like yours remind me why I started: connecting with thoughtful viewers like you matters so much more than view counts. You’ve given me a huge boost of motivation to keep creating. Thank you so much! ❤🙌✨

comments.author: @peterfillippsss
comments.text:
Hello again Epic Earth, i hope you have been well.
Thank you for another wonderful experience viewing and learning about somewhere on this planet we call home. The Yukon is certainly a very rugged and cold place. It must have been tough going for the early settlers in those regions. I must admit, it would be way too cold for me, i much prefer the warm to hot climate, love summers.
It must be very interesting making these documentaries as you would be gaining so much knowledge for yourself. The amount of detail that you cover is mind blowing to say the least.
I so look forward to your work as for me, it feels like i am taking a vacation each week, exploring what is outside of my known area.
Thank you so much again, take care of yourself and kind regards

replies.author: @EpicEarthYTB
replies.text: @peterfillippsss Thank you so much my dearest friend!!

replies.author: @peterfillippsss
replies.text:
@EpicEarthYTB Hello Epic Earth
It`s always nice to read your replies to my messages regarding your wonderful documentaries. Yes, you must be expanding your knowledge of the World by creating these. It`s kind of how i look on life, with each new day giving me the opportunity to expand my knowledge. Even if it`s something little and maybe irrelevant to many people, it`s a good feeling to keep learning. This is why i am so grateful to you for your work, as i find it all so interesting and visually spectacular. 

Now your question has got me a little stumped. As in all honesty, i don`t really have a place that i would love to travel to. Apart from one day wanting to see an active volcano would be very rewarding. 
It is certainly a question i may need to ponder over for a bit longer. 

I`ve seen snow on the ground when i was a young kid, but never saw it falling and think it would be nice to experience that if i was dressed warmly lol.

Take care of yourself and i look forward to seeing what amazing adventures await in your next documentary and as always, kind regards

replies.author: @EpicEarthYTB
replies.text:
Hello my friend! Seeing your message is always a highlight of my week. 🌿
The sheer contrast between the frozen expanses of the Yukon and the warm summer days you love is vast, but that is the wonder of our world! It's so humbling to reflect on how tough life must have been for those early settlers in the north.
Creating these documentaries is an ongoing education for me as well, and knowing you treat each episode as a window to explore beyond your daily horizons is profoundly rewarding.
I'm curious—given your love for warmer climates, where is one place in the world you would truly love to travel to if you had the chance?
Thank you for your warmth, loyalty, and inspiring mindset. Stay safe, take care of your health, and warmest regards as always! 🌊☀️🙏
